title: Annotatio II §.IX (1): Scripture — bread is called body, not body corporally present in the bread
pass_a_gloss: For Consubstantiation of whatever kind, even the Subtler — most of all Luther’s just recited, to be counted by us not unwillingly subtler, nay subtlest — is seen adverse: (1) By the express words of Scripture and of the Institution of the Sacred Supper itself, by which the bread indeed is said to be Christ’s body, but not Christ’s Body present to the bread, less corporally present to the bread, least of all corporally present in the bread itself. Certainly a Corporal presence of Christ’s body in the bread, besides that it imports Local presence insofar as it is called Corporal (Corporality ranging equally wide with Locality, at least intrinsic), also says inclusion, insofar as in the bread, though also outside it, Christ’s Body is alleged corporally present — and by that very fact the bread is not Christ’s Body, because Christ’s body is said only to exist corporally present in the bread.
pass_b_english: (1) Scripture and Institution say the bread is Christ’s body — not that the body is present to the bread, less corporally present to it, least of all corporally present in it.
Call presence corporal and you import locality and inclusion; then the bread is not the body, because the body is only said to exist corporally present in the bread.
source_text: Enimverò Consubstantiatio quæcunque etiam Subtilior, maximè Lutheri recitata modò, subtiliori utut, quin subtilissima, nobis haud invitis, accensenda, adversa conspicitur: (1) Expressis Scripturæ ipsiusque Institutionis Sacræ Coenæ verbis, quibus panis quidem corpus Christi dicitur esse, non autem Corpus Christi pani præsens, minus, pani corporaliter præsens, minimè omnium, in ipso pane, corporaliter præsens esse. Certè Corporalis præsentia corporis Christi in pane, præterquam quòd Localem præsentiam inferit, quatenus Corporalis esse dicitur (Corporalitate cum Localitate, saltem intrinseca, æquè latè patente) & inclusionem dicit, quatenus in pane, licèt & extra eum, Corpus Christi corporaliter præsens perhibetur, & eo ipso panis non est Corpus Christi, quia corpus Christi duntaxat in pane corporaliter præsens existere dicitur.

lemmas.gloss: the bread indeed is said to be Christ’s body
